    - paragraph: xᵢⱼ = units shipped from source i to destination j

    - text: All row supplies and column demands are satisfied. This is a feasible (valid) allocation.
    - article:
      - heading "MATHEMATICAL MODEL" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Let x₁₁, x₁₂, x₂₁, x₂₂ be the shipment variables.
      - heading "Constraints" [level=3]
      - term: Row (supply) constraints
      - definition: x₁₁ + x₁₂ = 30 (F1 supply) x₂₁ + x₂₂ = 20 (F2 supply)
      - term: Column (demand) constraints
      - definition: x₁₁ + x₂₁ = 25 (W1 demand) x₁₂ + x₂₂ = 25 (W2 demand)
      - term: Non-negativity
      - definition: xᵢⱼ ≥ 0 for all i, j
      - text: Objective (Minimize Total Cost)
      - paragraph: Minimize C = 4x₁₁ + 6x₁₂ + 5x₂₁ + 3x₂₂
    - article:
      - heading "COST SUMMARY" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Current Total Cost
      - status: ₹190
      - heading "Cost Breakdown" [level=3]
      - paragraph: "F1 → W1: 25 × ₹4 = ₹100"
      - paragraph: "F1 → W2: 5 × ₹6 = ₹30"
      - paragraph: "F2 → W1: 0 × ₹5 = ₹0"
      - paragraph: "F2 → W2: 20 × ₹3 = ₹60"
      - text: Total = ₹190
      - heading "Interpretation" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Total transport cost is the sum of units shipped × cost per unit over all routes.
    - heading "FEASIBLE ALLOCATIONS (One-Parameter Family)" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Let t = x₁₁. From constraints: x₁₂ = 30 − t, x₂₁ = 25 − t, x₂₂ = t − 5."
    - text: t = x₁₁
    - status "t = x₁₁ 25": "25"
    - slider "Feasible allocation t": "25"
    - text: 5 25 t = 5 → C = ₹270 t = 25 → C = ₹190 (Minimum)
    - heading "Cost as a function of t" [level=3]
    - paragraph: C(t) = 4t + 6(30 − t) + 5(25 − t) + 3(t − 5)
    - strong: C(t) = 290 − 4t
    - paragraph: Since the coefficient of t is −4, cost decreases as t increases. Minimum at t = 25 → minimum cost = ₹190.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISTAKE" [level=2]:

        - text: COMMON MISTAKE
      - text: Do not forget column constraints.
      - paragraph: Satisfying only row supplies may leave some warehouses under-served or over-served.
